scope_note: Each nonempty feature-list line and each open-ticket acceptance criterion has one result. Synthetic fixtures only. No classic instance, business data, migration execution, cutover or deployment. A pass applies only to its exact cited assertion.

features.heading: Customers and contacts
features.claim: Customers can be created manually without a CRM provider, searched locally, viewed as cards and opened in a detailed customer page. Administrators can create/edit/delete, import from enabled external CRM providers and request a sync. The provider layer supports HubSpot and a generic HTTP adapter; it is not necessary for manually managed customers. Provider badges/links, sync time/status/error and remote provider search/import appear in the UI.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Customers and contacts
features.claim: Customer information includes name, industry, website/domain, phone, description/notes, VAT/tax/company-registration identifiers, employee count, annual revenue, billing and visit address fields, hourly/LP rates, external provider/id/URL and timestamps. The detailed page includes contacts, associated projects/rate context, documents and offers. An optional optimize_customer AI action revises customer_notes for human review. The similarly named customer_rewrite handler generates issue-based report summaries and is not the customer-notes implementation.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Customers and contacts
features.claim: Contacts support name/email/phone/role/notes, multiple contacts, create/edit/delete and explicit promotion of a primary contact. The contacts table is canonical, while legacy customer contact fields are read/mirrored for compatibility. Customer deletion refuses customers with non-deleted assigned projects or ANY offer, including hidden offers.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Customers and contacts
features.claim: Customer/project documents can be uploaded, downloaded, labelled, given draft/active/expired status and validity dates, updated or deleted. Project cooperation metadata includes engagement/ownership/environment responsibility and SLA information; this is adjacent CRM scope rather than quote-document content.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Customer and offer numbers
features.claim: Creating a customer does not itself assign a customer number. The first offer allocates it in the same transaction as offer creation. New customer numbers use K + YYMM + a positive unpadded monthly sequence (e.g. K26091 is September 2026 sequence 1); month boundary is Europe/Vienna. A customer number is unique and normally immutable.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Customer and offer numbers
features.claim: Legacy numbers shaped KYY-NNN... can be explicitly converted once using the expected old number, only while every related offer remains draft. All draft customer-number snapshots and save revisions are updated atomically. A finalized offer blocks conversion. No automatic rewrite of existing numbers occurs. The conversion exists as an admin API; a dedicated button was not found in the inspected customer views.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Customer and offer numbers
features.claim: Offer numbers use AYYMMDD-NN (daily sequence, minimum two digits, Europe/Vienna). Creation allocates a unique offer number, even for a draft. Identity/customer association cannot later be changed. Sequences do not reuse hidden/deleted offer numbers.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Create and duplicate
features.claim: An administrator creates an offer from a customer. Missing sender prerequisites lead to settings. A new document takes sender and text defaults, current customer contact/address (billing address takes precedence), current Vienna date, 30-day validity, an initial quantity-1 position and default footer layout. These are snapshots, not live references to template content.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Create and duplicate
features.claim: Duplication copies the document of an offer for the SAME customer, creates a NEW offer id/number in draft and resets offer/valid-until dates. It refreshes customer email and uses the customer number. It does not copy accepted/sent state, public token, acceptance receipt, or delivery job. This is how classic revises a finalized offer.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Draft: editable by administrators; automatic/manual saving increments revision. Draft has no live customer capability.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Sent: the user has finalized the offer. Content is frozen, sent_at is recorded and a customer link is allocated. Finalization DOES NOT send an offer email. Distribution is manual through copied link, QR or PDF.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Accepted: the recipient expressly confirmed the current sent revision. The offer row and acceptance audit are immutable. Confirmation/PDF generation is asynchronous and does not make acceptance conditional on successful email delivery.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Expired: sent offer whose validity date is past (or invalid) is presented as expired on read. Expiry uses the Vienna calendar day; acceptance remains possible through the valid-until day. The stored status need not have been rewritten to expired. The customer can read but cannot accept.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Declined: allowed by the DB/status labels; no decline action/endpoint was found in the pinned quote implementation. Do not advertise an implemented reject workflow.
features.reason: Historical classic behavior or absent workflow; Aeon scope is traced separately in the open criteria.

features.heading: Status lifecycle
features.claim: Hidden/deleted: separate visibility flag. Drafts are described as deleted, finalized ones as archived; both can be restored or included in lists. It does not erase content/evidence, revoke an existing customer link or change commercial status.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Save, version and conflict behaviour
features.claim: Autosave is debounced about 700 ms; explicit Save and saved-at/saving/unsaved/error feedback are available. Save uses expected revision and only succeeds on a draft; stale writes or already finalized documents return 409. The UI keeps the local draft on conflict, permits a local draft download, and offers an explicit server reload that discards local changes. Save-before-navigation, before-unload warning and save-before-print/finalize protect local work. Invalid numeric inputs block save/print.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Save, version and conflict behaviour
features.claim: Revision is a monotonically increasing concurrency counter, NOT a retained series of draft snapshots or a user-selectable version history. Undo/redo is in the current document session. Finalized content is revised by duplication, not by editing or opening a newer version on the same offer.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Save, version and conflict behaviour
features.claim: PAI-1070 suppresses saves while loading/reloading, fences async responses to the current document and retains edits/selection through inspector interaction. Server prose writer guards protect newer structured/inline text from older editor versions, including settings writes inside a transaction.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Document content and pricing
features.claim: Users edit title, subtitle, project reference, date, expiry, recipient snapshot/address/contact, own contact person, introduction, ordered sections, positions, acceptance text and VAT wording directly on the page. The customer number remains immutable. The document uses an offer number and page X of Y footers.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Document content and pricing
features.claim: Up to 100 positions have short text, long text, quantity, unit and cent price. Rows can be added, selected, moved and removed. Server recalculates totals; quantity precision is two decimals, prices are nonnegative integer cents and each row rounds half-up to cents. EUR presentation and a textual VAT note are present; this is not a multi-currency/tax/invoice accounting engine. A default VAT note is not a computed tax amount.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Document content and pricing
features.claim: Finalization requires a title, customer name/address, at least one valid nonempty positive-quantity position, coherent dates, valid sender details and both sender/customer emails. Email and IBAN checks exist. Content becomes immutable on finalization.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Sections, lists and inline styles
features.claim: A document has up to 20 text sections with editable headings/body. Sections can be added, selected, reordered and deleted with modal confirmation. Heading/section numbering follows document order; the editor keeps selection and history associated with a section through moves/repagination.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Sections, lists and inline styles
features.claim: Prose supports paragraphs and list items, bullets (disc/circle/square/dash and plain custom glyph), decimal numbering and multilevel outline numbering. Depth 0..5 represents six displayed levels. Tab/Shift-Tab and inspector controls change level. Disabled level controls explain boundaries/limits. Start values up to 9999, restart, continuation across intervening paragraphs and section-bound versus independent numbering are supported. Generated numbers are not stored as part of the user's text.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Sections, lists and inline styles
features.claim: Marker horizontal/vertical positions and wrapped text start can be adjusted separately in mm (x -30..30; y -20..20; text -20..40). Numeric draft inputs tolerate incomplete typing and commit/canonicalize on completion; do not turn every keystroke into a forced clamp.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Sections, lists and inline styles
features.claim: Body prose supports independent bold and italic, together or separately, plus Normal to clear them. Controls reflect mixed selections and can set typing style at a caret, including composed characters. Styles are UTF-16 character ranges on plain text; no arbitrary HTML rich-text payload. Heading/cover OfferText fields remain plain text. There is no Tiptap/ProseMirror dependency in this feature. Classic bundles Manrope weights 400/500/600/700; italic is explicitly CSS-synthesized (font-synthesis: style), rather than a separately imported italic face.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Sections, lists and inline styles
features.claim: Up to 100 prose nodes/section and 2000 code points/node; strict normalization/validation on server and client. Legacy body strings still render; structured nodes supply a plain-body projection. Newer formatting requires writer version 3.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Inspector and document history
features.claim: The right-hand inspector has compact Text, Section and Document tabs with context-sensitive controls, inline formatting, list type/level/numbering/marker placement, section/position actions and footer layout. It can be hidden; the app header can be collapsed. It stacks at narrow widths. Selection is held while operating the inspector, so changes apply to the intended text rather than whichever element happens to have focus.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Inspector and document history
features.claim: Undo/redo covers document edits, section operations, position operations, prose and layout; moving a section and typing in it are not isolated incompatible histories. Template settings are clearly future-offer defaults and do not rewrite the open document.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Inspector and document history
features.claim: The selected footer mark can be resized 18..96 mm and offset vertically -6..10 mm in tenths. Existing legacy layout remains representable. Clicking the mark on a later page targets the clicked mark correctly. Embedded tenant-specific artwork and dimensions are not generic product content.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Keyboard/input behaviour
features.claim: Pos1/Home and End in prose and heading/plain fields move to the beginning/end of the VISUAL wrapped line; Shift extends selection. Native Selection.modify is preferred with a measured fallback preserving wrap affinity and scroll. Ctrl/Meta/Alt-modified Home/End are left to the browser. IME composition is protected.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Keyboard/input behaviour
features.claim: Ctrl/Cmd-B and -I change body-prose bold/italic. Ctrl/Cmd-Z undoes, Shift-Z or Ctrl/Cmd-Y redoes. Ctrl/Cmd-A selects the current prose editor. Enter splits paragraph/list structure, Shift-Enter inserts a soft break, Tab/Shift-Tab changes indentation, Backspace/Delete perform structured deletions. Paste is normalized to text rather than trusting HTML. Inspector tabs/radio groups/zoom menus support arrow/Home/End keys; modal dialogs trap normal browser focus and restore the trigger on close.
evidence: test:web/tests/quote-editor-input.spec.ts::plain paste, Unicode composition; web/tests/quote-inspector.spec.ts::bold and italic toggle

features.heading: Zoom, pagination and PDF
features.claim: Zoom supports Fit width, Fit page, percentage presets/stepping and typed 25..800%. Fit calculations use the actual stage and account for title bar/inspector size. Screen zoom must not affect physical print dimensions.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Zoom, pagination and PDF
features.claim: The renderer measures loaded fonts and content into A4 sheets (210 x 297 mm). Cover/sections paginate as whole blocks; positions start a separate section/page, tables repeat headings and the acceptance area moves as required. A block/row larger than one page produces an overflow warning and blocks print/finalize; it does not silently clip or split long prose across pages.

features.heading: Zoom, pagination and PDF
features.claim: Draft/finalized ordinary PDF export uses browser print from the dedicated print view. Public readers can print too. Accepted confirmation PDF is separately rendered server-side by headless Chromium/chromedp using the same Vue OfferDocument entry and stored durably; download becomes available when prepared. It includes an acceptance stamp, signer/company/time and hash reference. The old reports_pdf.go/fpdf engine is not the commercial offer renderer.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Zoom, pagination and PDF
features.claim: Server rendering uses an ephemeral loopback asset/payload server, restrictive CSP, isolated temporary browser state, stripped inherited environment, timeout and 20 MiB size limit. No production session is needed by the renderer.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Document settings
features.claim: An administrator can edit sender identity/address/contact/legal/bank fields and defaults for introduction, sections, acceptance and VAT wording. Changes apply to NEW offers; they do not silently update an existing draft or finalized document. Structured default prose is retained, and its plain textarea is read-only where nodes exist. Existing document footer/layout controls are separate.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Document settings
features.claim: The classic dialog falls back to bundled prototype-defaults.json when text defaults are empty. Its tenant-owned legal/commercial sections and company artwork must be omitted from the public port. Aeon should start neutral and allow tenant-owned configuration.
features.reason: No bundled tenant legal defaults or business artwork in the public quote renderer.

features.heading: Public link and QR acceptance
features.claim: Finalization creates a random 32-byte capability encoded base64url; a draft QR is explicitly a preview containing no functioning customer link. Finalized QR encodes the public /offers/:token page. A legacy finalized sent offer missing a token can receive one through explicit admin action. Copying/reading an existing link does not rotate it.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Public link and QR acceptance
features.claim: The capability holder can view the frozen document without signing in, print it and, while still valid/sent, accept. The form prefills contact/company, requires name, company and an explicit checkbox, allows a note, and sends the exact displayed revision. No signature image, identity proof or authenticated account is required by classic; possession of the link is authority. A second/stale acceptance returns conflict and cannot overwrite the first signer.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Public link and QR acceptance
features.claim: Acceptance atomically records time, entered identity/note, trusted-proxy-derived IP, limited user-agent, original document SHA-256 and offered revision; increments offer revision and seals it. Public JSON omits internal ids and audit IP/user-agent. Expired/accepted pages show the appropriate state without an active acceptance form.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Public link and QR acceptance
features.claim: Privacy middleware gives capability paths no-store/no-referrer/noindex headers. Public request code omits credentials; rate limits, JSON/custom-header checks and rejection of cross-site acceptance requests apply. Public access closes when CRM is explicitly disabled; ordinary authenticated CRM APIs are not switched off by this legacy UI setting. Archive does not revoke capabilities.
features.reason: The cited passing checks cover this source claim.

features.heading: Acceptance confirmation and notification
features.claim: New valid acceptances enqueue a durable confirmation; legacy accepted records are not automatically backfilled/sent. The same email goes to customer contact and sender (deduplicated if equal), includes accepted PDF and receipt/link. SMTP/PDF/public-base readiness is inspectable. Offer creator notices show the latest 20 accepted offers, rather than relying solely on transient notifications.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Acceptance confirmation and notification
features.claim: Queue states: pending, rendering, sending, sent, failed, uncertain. The dispatcher ticks every 5 seconds, retries safe failures with attempts-squared backoff (20 seconds multiplier) up to five attempts, and never automatically resends an ambiguous SMTP delivery. Admin retry requires explicit acknowledgement for uncertain state. UI also handles legacy/unavailable status; pending/rendering/sending receipts are refreshed about every 5 seconds. A failed email leaves the accepted document/receipt intact.
features.reason: The complete source claim needs direct integrated evidence.

features.heading: Collaboration: implemented versus requested terminology
features.claim: Implemented: optimistic concurrent save protection, a visible-page GET revision watch with 4/8/16/20-second backoff, immediate focus/visibility recheck, suppression of late/own-save responses, and an external-change notice. A clean document can be explicitly reloaded; dirty/in-flight work asks before replacement. PAI-1070 covers load/save races and maintains the local edit session. This is not operational-transform/CRDT simultaneous editing.
features.reason: Historical classic behavior or absent workflow; Aeon scope is traced separately in the open criteria.

features.heading: Collaboration: implemented versus requested terminology
features.claim: Not found in pinned quote/customer implementation: a per-offer active-user list, presence heartbeat endpoint, shared cursors or editing locks. offerProseSession.active is the active LOCAL editor target. App.vue's “active users” comment describes a five-minute login/session heartbeat, not collaborator presence. Searches covered offer components/view, v6 shell, App.vue, source filenames and active-users/presence terminology. Do not claim presence parity without a concrete source feature; implement it as the explicit new Aeon requirement in PAI-1067 under the 2026-09-24 scope.
